tasks.short: Monitor logistics standards and industry developments, then identify changes worth investigating.

steps.what: Check standards publishers and industry information services in {OTHER} for updates.
Read source documents and record relevant developments in {DOCS}.

loop.input: New source captures, previous versions and a fixed logistics topic list.
loop.output: Draft development notes with source passages, dates and links.
loop.check: Verify cited passages exist, dates match and every extracted claim has a source.
loop.stop: Process at most 20 documents per run with one repair attempt each; queue failures for manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Documents express changes in varied prose. Keyword alerts cannot reliably extract their scope.

steps.what: Compare developments with logistics performance and priorities in {SPREADSHEET}.
Prepare a monitoring brief with sources, implications and suggested investigations.
Discuss the brief and select investigations worth allocating time to.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} captures permitted updates and compares versions. A bounded extraction loop creates source-linked notes in {DOCS}; a {BI} view connects them to logistics measures from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The analyst judges local relevance, and a deterministic generator assembles the brief before the manager selects investigations in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources had different formats, update schedules and licensing terms. Maintaining a custom monitoring pipeline often cost more than periodic manual reading.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the effort of building collectors, version comparisons and brief templates. Bounded extraction can handle prose while retaining source passages for checking.
tasks.still_hard: Licensed standards may restrict copying. A published practice can be unsuitable for the company's routes, products or contracts.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which development changes a real operating constraint, and which apparent improvement will fail locally.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of small logistics improvement investigations.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time scanning sources and more time testing implications with operations. Proposed new authority is to initiate small, reversible investigations within an agreed time budget; larger commitments remain with the manager.

reach.task: Frame a logistics improvement investigation and compare options.
reach.learn: Baseline design, benefit estimation and distinguishing evidence from supplier claims.

reach.task: Prioritise changes across cost, service and resilience.
reach.learn: How operational trade-offs and investment limits shape priorities.

evidence.claim: Scheduled collection, version comparison and templated briefs can use deterministic technology; source interpretation still needs judgement.
The decomposition and build ranges are estimates, not measured results for this occupation.

assumptions: Monitoring uses a defined source register and permitted access methods.
The baseline covers public industry information rather than individual employee performance.
Build ranges cover a limited initial source set, access approval and rollout; they are not delivery guarantees.
unknowns: Which sources are subscribed to, licensed for processing and operationally important?
Which logistics measures and priorities are available in a usable form?
Who can authorise investigations, and what time budget can be delegated?
research_questions: Which relevant standards publishers provide permitted feeds or version histories?
How accurately can source-linked extraction distinguish proposals, guidance and binding requirements?
new_work: Maintain the source register and access permissions.
Read documents that fail extraction or source checks.
Correct relevance filters and remove repeated or promotional material.
Track whether selected investigations produced useful decisions.

tasks.short: Write and revise logistics procedures, validate them with operations, and publish approved versions.

steps.what: Collect existing procedures, incident records and process requirements from {DOCS}.
Walk through the process with operational staff and resolve undocumented practices.
Write the revised procedure in {DOCS}, including responsibilities, checks and exception handling.

loop.input: Approved template, current SOP, evidence pack and validated process notes.
loop.output: Draft SOP, change summary, source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check required sections, source references, named roles and consistency with validated notes; the analyst reviews the draft.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per revision; unresolved instructions remain flagged for the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure but cannot turn varied process notes into coherent instructions.

steps.what: Check draft instructions against actual operations and required controls.
Approve the validated procedure and its effective date.
Publish the approved version in {DOCS}, archive its predecessor and notify affected staff.

tasks.design: An integration gathers a versioned evidence pack from {DOCS} and the {OPS_SYSTEM}, and a bounded loop drafts a procedure from validated notes. Configured approvals in {WORKFLOW} record the supervisor's findings and the manager's approval of a specific version. That approved version is published in {DOCS}, with archiving and staff notifications handled automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual practice lived partly in people's heads. Templates helped formatting, but drafting, checking changes and managing versions still required manual coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can convert validated notes into a consistent procedure. AI coding makes evidence collection, change comparisons and document-control integrations cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent procedure may describe an impractical or unsafe process. Operational testing, specialist controls and agreement about responsibilities still take time.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the gap between written policy and real work, then agreeing instructions that staff can follow under pressure.

ambition.what: Incident-triggered procedure updates with a documented operational validation.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more of the week observing work and resolving ambiguous instructions. Proposed new authority is to open a controlled revision after a recurring incident and coordinate validation; the manager retains publication approval.

reach.task: Validate that a revised procedure addresses a recurring control failure.
reach.learn: Control objectives, evidence requirements and corrective-action verification.

reach.task: Test whether revised handoffs work during a busy shift.
reach.learn: Actual sequencing, queue constraints and exception paths.

evidence.claim: Document collection, version control, approval routing and publication can use deterministic workflows.
Drafting from approved process notes is suitable for a bounded model loop, with operational validation retained.

assumptions: A controlled SOP template, named approver and document versioning are available.
Only the exact approved version can be published automatically.
Incident records are minimised and access-controlled under GDPR.
Consent and access estimates include consultation under national rules where revised working methods require it.
The initial scope covers a small set of logistics procedures.
unknowns: Which procedures require safety, legal or quality specialist approval?
Which national consultation rules and collective agreements apply to changed working methods?
Can the document store enforce version-specific approval and archive access?
How much current practice is missing from existing records?
research_questions: Which draft defects are best detected through document checks versus operational walkthroughs?
Can the available document interfaces reliably bind approval to the published version?
new_work: Review drafts for unsupported instructions and missing exceptions.
Maintain templates, source references and role definitions.
Validate revised instructions during actual operations.
Handle failed publication, obsolete links and distribution changes.
Record consultation and specialist approvals where required.

tasks.short: Revise shipping schedules to consolidate loads, use capacity better and reduce empty movements.

steps.what: Review orders, vehicle capacity and current shipping schedules in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Compare load combinations and revised departure times in {SPREADSHEET}.
Check candidate schedules against service commitments and operating constraints in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Resolve timing and capacity conflicts with carriers and dispatchers by phone.
Approve and release the revised shipping schedule in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Send revised shipment instructions and record carrier acknowledgements through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Integrations create a current planning snapshot, and a configured optimiser in the {OPS_SYSTEM} generates feasible consolidation options. A comparison view exposes cost, utilisation, empty movements and service exceptions for analyst review. The dispatcher approves a specific schedule before configured notifications send its instructions through {PARTNER_PORTAL} or {EMAIL}, with missing acknowledgements returned as exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Optimisation already existed, but local constraints, carrier updates and order changes were expensive to connect and maintain. Spreadsheet planning often filled those gaps.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the effort of building connectors, constraint checks and comparison views around established optimisation software. No language model is needed for capacity arithmetic or schedule feasibility.
tasks.still_hard: Feasible plans depend on current capacity, realistic loading times and complete constraints. Disruptions and informal carrier commitments can invalidate an otherwise correct plan.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which commitment can move when capacity is scarce, and securing practical agreement from carriers and dispatchers.

ambition.what: Intraday consolidation decisions after material order or capacity changes.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time rebuilding schedules and more time resolving exceptions and comparing service trade-offs. Proposed new authority is to select the consolidation proposal within agreed cost and service limits; the dispatcher retains release authority.

reach.task: Resolve a disrupted departure plan and release workable shipment instructions.
reach.learn: Dispatch cut-offs, acknowledgement practices and the operational cost of late changes.

reach.task: Set trade-offs between utilisation, transport cost and delivery service.
reach.learn: How to set explicit limits and evaluate changes against realised outcomes.

evidence.claim: ORTEC documents route planning in a delivery operation, supporting configured optimisation as an available approach.
Shipment integration, deterministic constraint checks and version-specific release controls are technically feasible; local effort remains unvalidated.

assumptions: A suitable optimisation module can be configured and connected to the operations system.
The initial rollout covers one operating area and its principal carrier interfaces.
Configured constraints include applicable capacity, delivery-window and working-time requirements.
Notifications use only the released schedule version; material changes require another release.
Driver data is minimised under GDPR. Any employee evaluation requires assessment under the EU AI Act and applicable national rules.
Consent and access estimates include carrier permissions and employee consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Which optimisation capabilities and interfaces are already licensed?
How fresh and reliable are order, vehicle and carrier-capacity data?
Which physical, contractual and working-time constraints are currently undocumented?
Does using driver-level data trigger additional assessment or consultation under national rules?
What schedule-selection authority can be delegated to the analyst?
research_questions: How does the configured optimiser perform on representative local orders and disruptions?
What utilisation gains remain after checking actual loading, waiting and delivery times?
Which carrier interfaces support reliable acknowledgements and duplicate prevention?
new_work: Maintain capacities, rates, cut-offs and operating constraints.
Investigate infeasible plans and stale inputs.
Compare predicted savings with actual transport cost and delivery service.
Handle failed notifications and missing carrier acknowledgements.
Review access permissions and planning-data retention.

tasks.short: Ask potential suppliers about material availability and give buyers a reliable comparison.

steps.what: Check material requirements and potential supplier contacts in {PROCUREMENT}.
Check published stock and lead times in {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Send availability enquiries and follow up unanswered requests through {EMAIL}.
Read supplier replies and record quantities, dates and conditions.

loop.input: Supplier replies and attachments matched to the original item enquiry.
loop.output: Availability records with item, quantity, unit, date, conditions and supporting passages.
loop.check: Validate item matches, units and dates; flag contradictions and distinguish indicative stock from confirmed availability.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per reply; ambiguous or unmatched replies go to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier replies use varied prose and attachments. Fixed parsing cannot reliably capture conditional availability.

steps.what: Call suppliers to clarify uncertain availability, substitutions or delivery conditions.
Update the availability comparison in {SPREADSHEET} and pass it to the buyer.

tasks.design: An integration checks requirements in {PROCUREMENT} against fresh availability from {PARTNER_PORTAL}, suppressing enquiries already answered by sufficiently current data. Configured templates in {WORKFLOW} prepare nonbinding requests for analyst approval through {EMAIL}, and a bounded loop extracts replies into an availability register. The analyst clarifies uncertain commitments by phone, while a deterministic comparison gives the buyer quantities, dates, conditions and evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability was dispersed across portals, inboxes and phone conversations. Supplier formats and conditional promises made a single reliable comparison costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes enquiry tracking, portal connections and comparison records cheaper to build. Bounded extraction handles variable replies without trying to automate supplier relationships.
tasks.still_hard: Published stock can be stale, and a supplier's indication may not reserve material. Substitutions, urgent shortages and unfamiliar suppliers still require direct clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Testing how firm a supplier's promise is, finding workable alternatives and preserving trust during shortages.

ambition.what: A shared material availability register with evidence and expiry dates.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time chasing routine facts and more time validating scarce or uncertain supply. Proposed new authority is to select which availability claims need direct confirmation; supplier selection and purchase commitments remain with the buyer.

reach.task: Identify which missing materials threaten the production schedule.
reach.learn: Material criticality, acceptable substitutions and the latest useful delivery date.

reach.task: Assess whether a shortage needs another source or a schedule change.
reach.learn: Supply risk, qualification requirements and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Portal integrations, fixed enquiry templates, reminders and availability records can use deterministic technology.
Conditional supplier replies can use bounded extraction, while commercial clarification remains human.

assumptions: The initial scope covers a limited supplier set and permitted portal interfaces.
Enquiries are nonbinding and use approved specification fields and recipients.
The analyst approves a new enquiry's recipient and content before sending; bounded reminders reuse that approval.
Availability records retain source, timestamp, conditions and confirmation status.
Supplier contact data is access-controlled and retained under GDPR.
Consent and access estimates include mailbox permissions, supplier interface access and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which suppliers provide usable stock feeds or permitted portal access?
Which material specifications may be disclosed to which potential suppliers?
How long is each type of availability statement useful?
Who can approve substitutions or treat a supplier statement as a firm commitment?
How many current enquiries require phone clarification rather than a factual reply?
research_questions: How well does extraction distinguish stock indications, reservations and conditional delivery promises?
Which supplier interfaces provide timestamps and clear availability definitions?
new_work: Review ambiguous quantities, units, dates and conditions.
Maintain supplier contacts, enquiry templates and permitted disclosure fields.
Set expiry rules and refresh stale availability records.
Handle unanswered requests and failed portal connections.
Correct comparisons when suppliers revise earlier statements.

role.altitude: The role shifts towards frequent, evidence-backed decisions about logistics changes, schedule trade-offs and uncertain supply. Proposed authority expands to initiating small investigations and selecting feasible proposals within agreed limits; managers, dispatchers and buyers retain their respective approval rights.
reach: Management analysts: frame and evaluate operational improvement investigations.
Dispatchers: resolve schedule exceptions and prepare workable releases.
Quality control systems managers: validate procedures against actual controls.
Production, planning, and expediting clerks: connect material availability to schedule risk.
Supply chain managers: compare service, cost and resilience across alternatives.
skills_to_grow: Data quality, freshness and interface mapping.
Source verification and bounded model-output review.
Operational validation and controlled document changes.
Benefit measurement and small operational experiments.
GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and consultation under national rules.
role.ambitious_version: A logistics decision service that keeps current evidence, tests feasible alternatives and brings people a small set of actionable choices. The analyst leads investigations and exception resolution, with explicit delegated limits and approval attached to operational or commercial commitments.
